findings.aspect: How the client OBTAINS the referee server address written to LobbyManager+0x580 — the inbound NETMSG / client action that triggers the write, and the exact server_type/subtype values the stub must send.
findings.summary:
The referee address at LobbyManager+0x580 is OBTAINED via the lobby's standard AssignServer request/response, correlated by ticket_id. Mechanism (proven across SADK.exe build 34688 + tincat3.dll):

1) When LobbyManager state >= 6 (LoadingGlobalData onward), the per-frame LobbyManager_StatePump_Tick (FUN_00468f60 registration, decomp line 80321) installs callback FUN_004625d0 ("SetRefereeServerAddress") and calls pGameServerManager->vtbl[0x2c](4, 4) on the embedded LobbyServerList (this=LM+0x54, ServerList+0x6c = pGameServerManager).

2) pGameServerManager->vtbl[0x2c] = CommLayer::GameServerManager::AssignServer (tincat3 FUN_10021830 @ line 23937). It builds NETMSG 0xBD=189 (AssignServer), writes server_type=4 and server_subtype=4, registers a fresh ticket_id under category 0x108 (FUN_1002a1c0, storing an AssignServerTicketData), and sends it over the single lobby CommLayer (magic 0x26B6, port 7070). Guard at line 23950: AssignServer only accepts server_type in {3,4,5}.

3) The lobby must REPLY with NETMSG 0xAA=170 (GameServerData) carrying the SAME ticket_id, server_type=4, server_subtype=5, and the referee server's ip/port/server_id. Receive-side (tincat3 dispatch, switch on msg type @ line 25847; case 0xaa @ 26778): it resolves ticket_id -> category via FUN_1002a240; when category==0x108 it calls FUN_10021520 (@ line 23744), which gates on descriptor server_type==4 (desc+0x28) AND server_subtype==5 (desc+0x29) -> fires the referee-assigned observer callback with server_id.

4) That callback reaches SADK.exe FUN_004625d0 (decomp 78286-78300), which writes server_id to LM+0x580 (lines 78293/78297) and arms a 60000ms timer at +0x588 (disconnecting the old referee conn if the address changed).

5) Then FUN_00462910 (decomp 78499) — gated on *(LM+0x580)!=0 — resolves the server_id via LM->pComm (pComm->vtbl[0x38]/[0x18], lines 78510/78520) to an address and initializes RefereeServerConnection (LM+0x490), and the App per-frame loop calls RefereeServerConnection::Login(FUN_004793f0) which dials that address.

So: referee is ASSIGNED by the lobby via AssignServer(189, type=4, subtype=4) -> GameServerData(170, type=4, subtype=5) keyed by ticket_id. It is NOT TANConnectionRequest(223). server_type=4 = referee in this build; it is the ONLY AssignServer caller in all of SADK.exe (decomp line 83327 is the sole vtbl[0x2c] call). server_subtype is the second discriminator (request subtype=4, response subtype=5).

findings.wireFormat:
REFEREE ASSIGNMENT (over the lobby connection, port 7070, app magic 0x26B6, 28-byte TinCat frame header):

REQUEST (client -> lobby), NETMSG 189 = AssignServer (msgdefs [NETMSG_TYPE_189]):
  type        UNSHORT = 189
  server_type UNBYTE  = 4        (referee)
  server_subtype UNBYTE = 4      (request subtype; wire value from the (4,4) call)
  ticket_id   UNLONG  = T        (client-generated correlation id)

RESPONSE (lobby -> client), NETMSG 170 = GameServerData (msgdefs [NETMSG_TYPE_170]) — REQUIRED fields for the referee path:
  type           UNSHORT = 170
  server_id      UNLONG  = R     (any unique id; becomes LM+0x580, must be resolvable to ip:port by pComm)
  ip             STRING128 = <referee ip>     (OUR referee host)
  port           UNLONG    = <referee port>   (OUR referee port)
  server_type    UNBYTE  = 4     (MUST be 4)   <- FUN_10021520 gate desc+0x28
  server_subtype UNBYTE  = 5     (MUST be 5)   <- FUN_10021520 gate desc+0x29
  version        STRING32 = <referee proto/version string>
  room_id        UNLONG  = (per environment; referee likely ignores)
  ... (remaining 170 fields: name/owner_id/description/password_required/max_*/cur_*/ai_players/level/game_mode/hardcore/map/running/locked_config/data may be benign)
  ticket_id      UNLONG  = T     (MUST equal the request's ticket_id so it resolves to category 0x108)

ROUTING INVARIANTS (tincat3 dispatch FUN @ line 25839+):
  inbound msgType = (*msg)->vtbl[0x7c]()  -> must be 170 (0xAA)
  inbound ticket_id = (*msg)->vtbl[0x9c]()
  category = FUN_1002a240(pComm, ticket_id) -> must equal 0x108 (the category the client registered for AssignServer)
  => case 0xaa + category 0x108 -> FUN_10021520 -> if (server_type==4 && server_subtype==5) -> referee-assigned -> LM+0x580 = server_id

DESCRIPTOR (parsed 170) field offsets used by the gate: server_type @ desc+0x28, server_subtype @ desc+0x29 (also confirmed by SADK.exe AddOrUpdateDescriptor routing on desc+0x29; descriptor stride 0x5c).

PRECONDITION: the client first sends RegObserverServerList(171) for server_type=4 (and 5) at LoadingGlobalData; replying to those (or to the 170 itself) is what lets pComm cache server_id R -> ip:port so FUN_00462910's resolve (pComm->vtbl[0x18]/[0x38]) succeeds.

1) Add config: REFEREE_PORT (e.g. 5481, distinct from UC/WORLD/GAME) and reuse ADVERTISED_IP.

findings.aspect: RefereeServerConnection (LobbyManager+0x490) transport establishment: socket/port vs. shared 0x26B6 comm layer, framing, dial timing, the "connected" field, and what the Python stub must provide.
findings.summary: The RefereeServerConnection does NOT open a new TCP socket and does NOT use a separate port. It rides the SINGLE shared TinCat comm layer (the one and only `TinCat_CreateCommLayer(0,0x26B6,5,...)` at SADK.exe.c:79860 -> ICommLayer at LobbyManager+0x4c -> ConnectionManager `pComm` at LobbyManager+0x50), exactly like the Village and UserComm connections. Its init function FUN_00462910 (~78499) is byte-for-byte the same shape as LobbyManager::CreateVillageServerConnection (~79248): it calls pComm->vtbl[0x38](serverAddr) (Resolve), then pComm->vtbl[0x18](serverAddr) (build a connection descriptor/handle), then refConn->vtbl[+4](descriptor) which is LobbyBaseConnection::Init (FUN_0048de70 @112577) that merely stores the comm-issued handle at refConn+0x34. All five lobby sub-connections derive from `.\LobbyBaseConnection.cpp` and multiplex over the one comm layer; inbound data is routed to the right sub-connection by comparing connId to conn+0x34 (FUN_0048dd30 @112498: `*(conn+0x34)==connId`). Framing is therefore identical to the lobby: 28-byte TinCat header + app magic 0x26B6, and referee message bodies are TinCat PropertySet (named-field) bodies (FUN_0048f490(\"GameID\"/\"Result\"...) + reader vtbl[0x18](dst,0x20)) wrapped in a SendGameData-style NETMSG envelope — the same mechanism the village 1000-series uses. Dial timing is two-phase: (a) the referee server address must first be populated at LobbyManager+0x580 by callback FUN_004625d0 (also sets a 60000ms keep-alive at +0x588) when the lobby/room server tells the client the referee endpoint; (b) thereafter, EVERY FRAME once LobbyManager.state>=6, the StatePump tick (LobbyManager_StatePump_Tick @80246, lines 80332-80334) checks refConn->vtbl[0x2c]() (IsConnected) and, if false AND *(LM+0x580)!=0, calls FUN_00462910 to Resolve+bind the transport. RefereeServerConnection::Login (FUN_004793f0 @96425) is fired separately on NE_StartLoading (gameobj+0x3cc set, LM+0x3625=1) from the menu loop (~46178-46185), retried up to 5x ([Reconnector] timesClientRetries=5) then the match ABORTS; Login only sends if refConn+0x34!=0 (i.e. transport already bound) via transport->vtbl[0x10](msg,...). CONCLUSION FOR THE STUB: NO new listener port is required. The referee is just another logical connection multiplexed on the existing lobby/UC/village 0x26B6 transport, distinguished by connId. The stub must (1) advertise/deliver a referee-server endpoint so the client sets LM+0x580 (otherwise FUN_00462910 no-ops and logs \"Could not initialize RefereeServerConnection.\"), (2) accept the referee connection's login over the same 0x26B6 framing, and (3) push a LoginSuccess so the StartLoading referee-login retry succeeds and the match is allowed to start.

findings.wireFormat:
Transport: ONE TinCat connection, 28-byte TinCat frame header + app magic 0x26B6 (identical to lobby/UC/village). No separate referee socket or port. Referee is one logical connection multiplexed on the shared comm layer, demultiplexed by connId (== conn+0x34). 

Referee init sequence (FUN_00462910, mirrors village; addresses are build-34688 VAs):
  pComm = *(LobbyManager+0x50)            ; the single ConnectionManager
  serverAddr = *(LobbyManager+0x580)      ; referee endpoint, set by FUN_004625d0
  resolveRC = pComm->vtbl[0x38](serverAddr)               ; Resolve; OK iff ==0 or ==0xCD
  desc      = pComm->vtbl[0x18](serverAddr)               ; build connection descriptor/handle
  ok        = refConn(LM+0x490)->vtbl[+4](desc)           ; LobbyBaseConnection::Init -> conn+0x34 = desc
  ; failure -> log '.\\LobbyManager.cpp' 'Could not initialize RefereeServerConnection.'

Connect (LobbyBaseConnection::Connect, vtbl[0xC], FUN @0x48...:112648): if conn+0x34==0 return false; else transport=*(conn+0x34); transport->vtbl[0x1c](connectParams) to initiate connect/login.

IsConnected (vtbl[0x2c] body FUN_0048dd00): conn+0x34!=0 AND (*(conn+0x34))->vtbl[0xC]() in (0, !{8,9}).

Login PDU (RefereeServerConnection::Login FUN_004793f0): builds a PropertySet body (named fields, e.g. seen GameID/Result via FUN_0048f490(name) + memblock 0x20) and sends via transport->vtbl[0x10](msg,0,...). findings.recommendationForStub: Do NOT add a new listener port for the referee. The RefereeServerConnection is proven to multiplex over the existing single 0x26B6 TinCat comm layer (same 28-byte header + 0x26B6 magic), demultiplexed by connId — there is exactly one TinCat_CreateCommLayer in the whole client and all sub-connections (lobby/UC/village/referee) ride it. Concretely, the stub should: (1) Deliver a referee-server endpoint to the client so it populates LobbyManager+0x580 (via the message FUN_004625d0 handles). If the client is fine reusing the existing connection, the referee will Resolve+bind over it; if Resolve insists on a distinct ip:port, point it at the SAME stub host on a 0x26B6-speaking socket (open question 3). Without this, FUN_00462910 no-ops and logs 'Could not initialize RefereeServerConnection.' and — because StartLoading then retries Login 5x and ABORTS — no match can start. (2) When the referee connection logs in (RefereeServerConnection::Login fires on StartLoading), reply with the referee LoginSuccess PropertySet so refConn+0x34 stays bound and IsConnected (FUN_0048dd00) reports true, satisfying the per-frame StatePump retry and the menu-loop login gate. (3) Implement the referee request/response messages as TinCat PropertySet bodies (named fields like GameID/Result, 0x20-byte MEMBLOCKs) reusing the village.py PropertySet machinery and the same GameData NETMSG envelope, NOT as new msgdefs.ini schema types. Net: the referee is a 'virtual' connection on the lobby transport — the work is message handling + endpoint advertisement, not a new socket/port.

findings.aspect: RefereeServerConnection LOGIN exchange (the handshake that must succeed to stop the 5x-retry match abort) — what Login sends, what inbound message fires LoginSuccessReceived vs LoginFailedReceived, and exactly what the stub must emit.
findings.summary: RefereeServerConnection::Login (FUN_004793f0 @~96425) does NOT build/send an application "login" NETMSG or property-bag. It opens a TinCat data channel on the referee connection's transport: `this->pTransport->vtbl[0x10](commSystem, 0)` (pTransport = refConn+0x34, set in init FUN_00462910 to the per-address connection object for the referee server at LM+0x580). vtbl+0x10 is the same "Open/JoinChannel" call used by UserCommConnection::OpenCommunication (FUN_004793f0's twin at line 101743, annotated "Open/JoinChannel on this+0x34"); it returns 0 on success and the only thing Login does with a non-zero result is log it as an error. So login is server-driven: once the client opens the referee channel, the REFEREE SERVER (the stub) must PUSH an inbound message that the referee-conn dispatcher (FUN_0047b090) decodes. That dispatcher switches on the LobbyMessage id: id 0xdca (3530) -> LoginSuccessReceived (FUN_0047ac20), id 0xdcb (3531) -> LoginFailedReceived (FUN_0047ad50). The verdict is the MESSAGE ID, not an errorcode field: LoginSuccessReceived reads exactly one field "PermID" (u32, read-and-discard into a stack local) then fires the connection's observer fan-out (FUN_00479ef0); LoginFailedReceived is byte-for-byte the same except it logs at line 0x20b and is reached only by id 0xdcb. Neither reads an errorcode and neither inspects PermID's value. THEREFORE: to make login succeed and stop the abort, the stub (acting as referee server) sends a LobbyMessage with category=3, id=0xdca, containing a single property "PermID"=the player's perm_id. To avoid failure, never send id 0xdcb. The retry/abort loop (FUN_00435980 @46171-46201) keeps game+0x3624[+1]=0xd89 "referee-login-pending" set and ABORTS the match (FUN_00429900(2)/FUN_0042a640) once attempts(0xd8b)>=5; success must clear 0xd89 via the observer fan-out that LoginSuccessReceived triggers.
findings.wireFormat:
REFEREE TRANSPORT: rides the single TinCat comm layer (ConnectionManager = *(LM+0x50); resolve via vtbl+0x38, get-connection via vtbl+0x18) to a DISTINCT server address held at LM+0x580. Same 28-byte TinCat frame header + app magic 0x26B6 as lobby/UC. NOT the village SendGameData(74) envelope — referee msgs are bare LobbyMessages (tincat3 PropertyDataConverter bit-stream), unlike the stub's EnterWorld(1000) which is wrapped in SendGameData(74).

LOBBYMESSAGE HEADER (from constructor FUN_0048fb00(this, cat=3, id, size) and reader FUN_0048fa50(this, typeWord, transport)):
- msg+0x24 (param[9]) = category = 3 for all referee messages.
- msg+0x28 (param[10]) = message id (the value FUN_0048eef0 returns and the dispatcher switches on): Login OK=0xdca, Login FAIL=0xdcb. (Family: ClaimChest req 0xdac -> Ack 0xdad/Result 0xdae; RegisterGame req 0xdb6 -> 0xdb7/0xdb8; GiveUp 0xdc1/0xdc2; FinishGame ...; Logout. Send-side built with FUN_0048fb00(3, 0xdac/0xdb6/..., size).)
- The on-wire TYPE WORD is 16-bit: bits 11-0 = id (max 0xfff; 0xdca fits), bits 14-12 = category (=3), bit15 = NAMES-PRESENT flag. Reader sets msg+0x20 (= param[8], the "include field names" flag) = (typeWord>>15)&1. So the combined type word for LoginSuccess = (3<<12)|0xdca = 0x3dca with names off, or 0xbdca with names on.

FIELD SERIALIZATION (PropertyDataConverter, FUN_0048f490 select-name + FUN_0048f2c0 write-u32 / reader vtbl+0x18 read-u32, width 0x20=32 bits):
- IF msg+0x20 (names flag) != 0: each field writes its NAME (FUN_0048f490->FUN_00762400(name)) then a type tag FUN_00762400(1) + width FUN_00762400(0x20) then the 32-bit value (FUN_0048ef70). Body is name-keyed.
- IF msg+0x20 == 0: ONLY the 32-bit value bits are written, NO names, NO type tags. Body is positional; the reader's FUN_0048f490("PermID") becomes a no-op and values are read in order.
- LoginSuccess(0xdca) body = exactly one property: PermID (UNLONG / u32). LoginFailed(0xdcb) body = same one PermID field (no error string in the receiver). The bit-stream is byte-aligned/flushed by FUN_0048f4c0/FUN_0048f530 (writes a 0xfff end-marker + bit count when names are on).

LOGIN REQUEST WIRE: none at the application layer — it is the TinCat channel-open (pTransport->vtbl[0x10](handle,0)). No perm_id/token/gameid is sent by Login itself.

findings.aspect: Referee protocol AFTER successful login: post-login ordered sequence, and the MINIMAL mandatory reply set to clear the match-start (loading) gate vs optional end-of-match/ranking messages.
findings.summary: The match-start gate is driven ENTIRELY by referee LOGIN, not by RegisterGame/FinishGame/ClaimChest. NE_StartLoading handler FUN_004316c0 (@line 42955) sets the master "referee-login-pending" flag LM+0x3624(=1) and "do-login" flag LM+0x3625(=1), retry-count LM+0x362c=0, frame-countdown LM+0x3628=0x10. The per-frame loop (lines 46171-46201) reads LM+0x3624; while set and attempts<5 (LM+0x362c), it dispatches RefereeServerConnection::Login = FUN_004793f0 (@96425) on the referee conn (LM+0x490, target=commSystem) and clears LM+0x3625; if attempts reach 5 it ABORTS the match (46193: clears LM+0x3624/0x3625, tears down). So the SOLE mandatory thing the stub must do to clear the loading gate is accept the referee login and reply LoginSuccess (msg 0xdca/3530), NOT LoginFailed (0xdcb/3531). Both LoginSuccessReceived (FUN_0047ac20, case 0xdca) and LoginFailedReceived (FUN_0047ad50, case 0xdcb) parse a 'PermID' field and fire the 'login-completed' observer fan-out FUN_00479ef0; the SUCCESS path is what lets the loading sequence proceed (LoginFailed leads to retry/abort). The referee message router is FUN_0047b090 (@97651): switch on msgtype extracted by FUN_0048eef0. RegisterGame (send 0xdb6/3510, FUN_00479840 built by FUN_00432240 @43442) is NOT auto-sent on LoginSuccess and is NOT polled by the loading gate; it is a GAME-STATE-machine callback (registered via FUN_004324e0/FUN_00458860 at 44826/45812). On the HOST it carries map/avatar data and its Result (0xdb8/3512, FUN_0047a580) returns the 'GameSeed' (needed for deterministic sim) via the success fan-out FUN_00464300; on failure it calls the abort fan-out FUN_00479e10 ('RegisterGameFailed'). FinishGame(0xdc0/3520) + Ack(0xdc1) + Result(0xdc2), GiveUpGame(0xdd4/3540)+Ack(0xdd5), ClaimChest(0xdac/3500)+Ack(0xdad)+Result(0xdae) are ALL end-of-match / mid-match settlement and are NOT on the start-loading path. The 252/253 GameResultSubmit and 254-257 ranking NETMSGs do not appear anywhere in the RefereeServerConnection code and are a SEPARATE subsystem (none referenced by referee handlers). NOTE: referee messages are NOT in msgdefs.ini — they are TinCat PropertySet bodies with hardcoded named fields built by FUN_0048fb00(channel=3, msgtype, size).

findings.wireFormat:
Referee messages ride the single TinCat comm layer (28-byte frame header, app magic 0x26B6) but their BODIES are TinCat PropertySet (positional named-field) bodies, NOT msgdefs NETMSG types (they are absent from msgdefs.ini). Each is built by FUN_0048fb00(channel=3, msgtype, reservedSize) then a series of FUN_0048f490("FieldName",0) + value writers (FUN_0048f2c0=u32/0x20-bit int, FUN_0048f440=byte buffer, FUN_0048fe20=string, FUN_0048f3c0=bool, FUN_0048f1c0=byte). Receivers parse via vtbl+0x18 (read named int) / vtbl+0x30 (read named string), keyed by FUN_0048eef0 (msgtype) in router FUN_0047b090.

MESSAGE ID TABLE (decimal = hex):
  SEND (client->referee):
    ClaimChest    = 3500 (0xdac): GameID(u32), MapGUID(16B), ActorID(u32), ChestID(u32)
    RegisterGame  = 3510 (0xdb6): GameID(u32), MapGUID(16B), MapName(str), MapSettings(str), RankedGame(bool), Wager(u32), AIPlayer(byte/8b), AvatarID x6 (u32 each)
    FinishGame    = 3520 (0xdc0): GameID(u32), MapGUID(16B), MapSettings(str), Winner(u32)
    Login         = 3529 (0xdc9)? [HYPOTHESIS — Login uses conn->vtbl[0x10] login primitive, not an explicit FUN_0048fb00(0xdc9); ID inferred by the +1/+2 pattern of the Ack/Fail pair below]
    GiveUpGame    = 3540 (0xdd4): GameID(u32), MapGUID(16B)
  RECV (referee->client), routed by FUN_0047b090 switch:
    3500..? ClaimChestAck    = 3501 (0xdad) FUN_00479fb0: GameID, Result  (Result==0 => 'waiting for other players to send claim info')
    ClaimChestResult         = 3502 (0xdae) FUN_0047a160: AvatarID, ChestID, <unnamed str>  (=> ClaimChestOK/Failed)
    RegisterGameAck          = 3511 (0xdb7) FUN_0047a3d0: GameID, Result  (Result==0 => 'waiting for other players to report start of game')
    RegisterGameResult       = 3512 (0xdb8) FUN_0047a580: GameID, Result; if Result==0 -> GameSeed(u32) [success, fan-out FUN_00464300]; else FailReason(str) [abort FUN_00479e10]
    FinishGameAck            = 3521 (0xdc1) FUN_0047a810: GameID, Result
    FinishGameResult         = 3522 (0xdc2) FUN_0047a9c0: GameID, Result; Result==0 -> FUN_00464300; else FailReason(str)
    LoginSuccess             = 3530 (0xdca) FUN_0047ac20: PermID(read via vtbl+0x18, 0x20-bit) -> fan-out FUN_00479ef0  [THE match-start clearer]
    LoginFailed              = 3531 (0xdcb) FUN_0047ad50: PermID -> fan-out FUN_00479ef0 (failure)
    GiveUpGameAck            = 3541 (0xdd5) FUN_0047ae80: (reads fields; logs GiveUpGameFailed on Reason)
Field name semantics for Result: 0 = OK/success; non-zero = error code (logged via 'XxxFailed: %d').

findings.recommendationForStub:
MINIMAL mandatory set to clear the match-start (loading) gate = exactly ONE referee reply: accept the referee LOGIN and answer with LoginSuccess (msg 0xdca/3530) carrying a PermID field. This is the only thing the per-frame loading loop (lines 46171-46201) waits on; a LoginSuccess within the 5-attempt window clears LM+0x3624/0x3625 and lets loading proceed, while LoginFailed (0xdcb) or no reply leads to retry then match ABORT. Implement: stand up the referee endpoint (ensure the address that lands in LM+0x580 is advertised so FUN_00462910 inits the conn), accept the inbound referee login frame on the shared 0x26B6 TinCat transport, and immediately reply 0xdca with PermID (echo the player's lobby/UC permId for safety). Do NOT reply 0xdcb. 

SECOND-TIER (send only if the host actually emits these — they are NOT polled by the loading flag but DO gate the host's game-state machine): if you receive RegisterGame (0xdb6/3510), reply RegisterGameAck (0xdb7, Result=0) then RegisterGameResult (0xdb8/3512) with Result=0 and a GameSeed (any deterministic u32, e.g. a fixed or per-match value) — the host needs the seed to start the deterministic simulation and otherwise sits at 'waiting for other players to report start of game'. 

CAN BE STUBBED/DEFERRED (end-of-match / settlement / ranking — none affect start): FinishGame 0xdc0 + Ack 0xdc1 + Result 0xdc2 (reply Result=0 to cleanly end), GiveUpGame 0xdd4 + Ack 0xdd5, ClaimChest 0xdac + Ack 0xdad + Result 0xdae. The GameResultSubmit (252/253) and ranking (254-257) NETMSGs are a different subsystem entirely (absent from the referee code and from msgdefs.ini) and require no referee handling at all for a match to start or run. 

IMPORTANT: referee messages are PropertySet bodies (FUN_0048fb00 channel=3 + named fields), NOT msgdefs NETMSG types — the stub's referee codec must build/parse positional named-field PropertySet bodies, not go through the msgdefs codec path. All of this is read-only protocol modeling; emitting LoginSuccess is the genuine mechanism the client is waiting for, not a forced bypass — but any change to the stub's wire behavior to implement it is a MUTATION and per HARNESS.md requires a user-approved Engagement Record before flipping it on.

findings.summary:
PART A: All 14 requested msgdefs.ini layouts extracted verbatim (see wireFormat). They are the POSITIONAL NETMSG schema used by the lobby/UC connections; the existing codec.encode_body/decode_body already drives them straight from the registry, so no new codec work is needed for these 14.

PART B — CRITICAL ARCHITECTURE FINDING: the Referee server is NOT a positional-NETMSG server like lobby/UC. The decomp (.\\LobbyRefereeServerConnection.cpp) shows RefereeServerConnection speaks the SAME named-property PropertySet protocol as the village/world layer: every referee request is built with FUN_0048fb00(category=3, msg_type, size) + FUN_0048f490(\"PropName\",0) + typed writers, e.g. RegisterGame(FUN @96636) = msg_type 0xDB6 with properties GameID/MapGUID/MapName/MapSettings/RankedGame/Wager/AIPlayer/AvatarID×6; ClaimChest=0xDAC, FinishGame=0xDC0, GiveUpGame=0xDD4. Replies LoginSuccessReceived/LoginFailedReceived read named props (\"PermID\" via vtbl+0x18 ReadMemBlock 0x20). These referee msg_types (~0xDAC-0xDD4, 3500-3540) are NOT in msgdefs.ini (which only covers positional NETMSG 1-262). So the 14 layouts in Part A are the SURROUNDING lobby/assign/result machinery (how the referee gets discovered + ACKed), while the referee's OWN traffic rides the village-style PropertySet/SendGameData(74) envelope.

Consequently the TEMPLATE to copy is the VILLAGE/WORLD connection (is_village path: framing + raw capture + the SendGameData(74) PropertySet handling in dispatch._h_send_game_data / village.py), PLUS the address-assignment wiring of _h_assign_server (189->192) and _h_connection_data (221->222). Concrete file/function plan is in recommendationForStub.

ADDRESS DELIVERY (PROVEN, build 34688): the referee conn object = LM+0x490, its server address = LM+0x580. FUN_00462910 (@78499) inits it only if *(LM+0x580)!=0 else logs \"Could not initialize RefereeServerConnection.\". The address is stored by setter FUN_004625d0 (@78286, also sets a 60000ms timeout at LM+0x588). The per-frame update (@80318) registers that setter as a server-resolution callback via FUN_00468f60(this, FUN_004625d0) once LobbyManager->state>5 (Authorized), through *(*(LM+0x6c)+0x2c)(4,4) logged from .\\LobbyVillageServerList.cpp — i.e. the referee address is resolved through the SAME server-address channel the village list uses. On NE_StartLoading the client sets the \"do referee login\" flag (LM+0x3625=1) and the loop (@46171-46200) calls Login (FUN_004793f0 @46184), retrying <5 then ABORTING the match — so referee login MUST succeed.
